overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the board member's device messages were not "used" at the May 27 meeting because they were neither identified nor discussed. Public records claims were declined and referred to the Supervisor of Records.

allegations.summary: A board member allegedly used text messaging during a Zoom meeting, and the messages she referenced were not made public, so they should be released as meeting documents.
allegations.key_passage: those items do not constitute documents or exhibits “used” at the meeting for purposes of the Open Meeting Law, as they were not verbally identified nor their contents discussed

allegations.summary: The complainant alleged that the board member's text messages are public records subject to disclosure under the Public Records Law.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review such allegation as the Division of Open Government enforces and interprets the Open Meeting Law only
